seo.title: Do Press Releases Help AI Search? An Honest Answer
seo.meta_description: Do press releases help AI search? What wire distribution does and does not do, when releases are worth it, how to write one AI can use, and better options.

h1: Do Press Releases Help AI Search? When They Work and When They Don't
answer: Press releases help AI search only in limited ways. A release on your own site can give AI tools an official, dated statement of facts, and genuine news can lead journalists to write independent coverage, which matters more. Mass wire distribution to low-quality sites rarely helps, and press releases created mainly for links fall under Google's link scheme concerns.
key_takeaways: A release on your own site documents official facts and dates.
Independent coverage that follows a release matters most.
Mass distribution to low-quality sites adds little.
Releases created for links can breach Google's policies.
Real news, clear facts and a quotable spokesperson make releases useful.

sections.heading: What a press release can do
sections.body_html: A press release is an official statement of news: a launch, an acquisition, a study, a new location. Published on your own site, it gives search engines and AI tools a dated, authoritative source for those facts. When the news is genuinely interesting, it can prompt journalists to write their own articles, and that independent coverage is far more valuable than the release itself.

sections.heading: What it usually does not do
sections.body_html: Distributing a release through a wire service often results in many copies on syndication sites that few people read. Those copies are duplicates, not independent coverage. They rarely change how AI tools describe a business. Google's spam policies list link schemes, and press releases distributed mainly to build links are among the practices search engines discount.

sections.heading: When a release is worth it
sections.body_html:
• You have real news that affects customers, partners or your industry.
  • You are publishing original research or data.
  • You need an official record of a significant change, such as a merger, rebrand or new leadership.
  • You are announcing something local media are likely to care about.

sections.heading: How to write a release AI can use
sections.body_html:
1. Headline that states the news plainly.
  2. First paragraph: who, what, when, where and why, in two or three sentences.
  3. Specific facts: numbers, dates, names, locations.
  4. A quote that adds insight, not just enthusiasm.
  5. Boilerplate: one consistent description of the company.
  6. Contact details for media.

A release written like this is easy for journalists to use and gives AI tools clear facts.

sections.heading: Publish it on your own site first
sections.body_html: Keep a newsroom or press page with every release, dated and in text. This becomes the canonical source of your official announcements. Link related service or About pages to it where relevant, and update your About page when a release changes key facts.

sections.heading: Pitch, do not just distribute
sections.body_html: Send the news directly to a small list of relevant journalists, editors and newsletter writers with a short, personal note explaining why it matters to their readers. A few targeted pitches to local and trade publications usually produce better coverage than broad distribution.

sections.heading: Better alternatives for AI visibility
sections.body_html:
• Original data that journalists can cite.
  • Expert commentary through journalist request platforms.
  • Guest articles in relevant trade publications.
  • Podcast appearances in your niche.
  • Local community involvement that earns local news.

Each produces independent mentions that AI tools treat as corroboration.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Releases about non-news, such as minor website updates.
  • Vague, adjective-heavy writing with no facts.
  • Keyword-stuffed anchor links in the release body.
  • Different company descriptions in every release.
  • Paying for distribution and counting syndicated copies as coverage.

sections.heading: How to measure
sections.body_html: Count independent articles written by journalists, not syndicated copies. Track referral traffic from coverage, branded search after announcements and whether AI tools mention the news when asked about your company. If a release produced no independent coverage, the lesson is usually about the news value or the pitch, not the distribution channel.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: A press release is a record, not a ranking tactic. Use it for real news, write it with clear facts, publish it on your site and pitch it to the right journalists. Independent coverage is what helps AI search.

sections.heading: An example of real news versus non-news
sections.body_html: "Local agency publishes study of 200 Orange County business websites, finding most block at least one AI search crawler" is news: it is new, specific and relevant to local business readers. "Local agency launches redesigned website" is not, unless something about it affects customers. The first can earn coverage in regional business news and trade newsletters; the second will mostly be ignored, however widely it is distributed.

sections.heading: Newsroom page essentials
sections.body_html: A good newsroom page lists releases in date order with clear headlines, offers a one-paragraph company description and fact sheet, provides logos and leadership photos for download, names a media contact with email and phone, and links to notable coverage. Journalists use it to check facts quickly, and AI tools can use it as an official, dated source.

sections.heading: Timing and follow-up
sections.body_html: Send news when journalists can use it: early in the week, avoiding major holidays, and with enough lead time for publications with fixed deadlines. Follow up once, briefly, with any new detail, then move on. If a journalist covers the story, thank them, share the article and keep them in mind for future news.

sections.heading: Checklist before sending
sections.body_html:
• Is this genuinely news to someone outside the company?
  • Does the first paragraph state who, what, when, where and why?
  • Are the facts specific and correct?
  • Is the boilerplate identical to your About page?
  • Is it published on your newsroom page?
  • Do you have a short list of relevant journalists to pitch personally?

faqs.q: Do press releases help AI search?
faqs.a: Only in limited ways. A release on your site documents official facts, and real news can lead to independent coverage, which matters most. Mass distribution rarely helps.

faqs.q: Do press release links help SEO?
faqs.a: Links in widely distributed press releases are generally discounted, and releases created mainly for links can fall under Google's link scheme concerns.
It can help reach journalists for major news, but syndicated copies are not independent coverage. Targeted pitches often work better.

faqs.q: How should a press release be written for AI?
faqs.a: State the news plainly, put who, what, when, where and why first, include specific facts, a useful quote and consistent boilerplate.

faqs.q: Where should I publish press releases?
faqs.a: On your own newsroom or press page first, dated and in text, as the official source.

faqs.q: What is better than a press release for AI visibility?
faqs.a: Original data, expert commentary, guest articles, podcasts and local involvement that earn independent mentions.

faqs.q: How do I measure a press release?
faqs.a: Count independent articles by journalists, referral traffic, branded search and whether AI tools mention the news.

faqs.q: How often should a business send press releases?
faqs.a: Only when there is genuine news. Frequent releases about minor updates reduce attention for the ones that matter.
Include a link to your site or the relevant page for readers, but do not stuff releases with keyword-rich links; they are generally discounted.

faqs.q: Can a press release correct wrong information in AI answers?
faqs.a: An official, dated release on your own site can help document corrected facts, especially after a rebrand, move or leadership change.

faqs.q: Are paid press release placements on news sites worth it?
faqs.a: Paid placements that are labeled as press releases are not independent coverage, so they carry little weight with readers or AI tools.
